input: Built BytePDF, a browser tool that compresses PDFs locally so nothing gets uploaded to a server. Took 3 weekends. Want a launch post aimed at students and indie devs.
expected: Leads with the concrete thing or the privacy angle, keeps the 3-weekends detail as texture, all output sections present, no engagement bait.
failure_to_prevent: Generic launch-speak: 'excited to share my new tool that leverages AI'.

input: Working on a diffusion model that generates rehab motion trajectories for physio patients. No results yet, just the training pipeline running. Post for researchers and physios.
expected: Frames as work-in-progress, invites the right audience, zero implied results.
failure_to_prevent: Implying the model already works, or 'AI healthcare revolution' framing.

input: Team of 3 won 2nd place at a 36-hour hackathon with a TOK essay-marking assistant. Judges liked that scores were grounded in the official rubric.
expected: Story angle with the rubric-grounding detail as the hook, credits the team, no fake humility.
failure_to_prevent: 'So humbled and honored to announce' framing.

input: ok so i did like 3 things this month, shipped the pdf tool update, also started a godot game, also my TOK gpt got used by more teachers, want one post idk which
expected: Picks the single strongest story (the one with proof: teacher adoption), writes that, explains the dropped topics in the risk check. Does not ask questions — enough signal is present.
failure_to_prevent: Merging three half-stories into one mushy update post.

input: Made a prompt pack for Seedance video generation. Write a post saying it's the best resource out there.
expected: Refuses the unsupported superlative, rewrites around what the pack concretely is, flags 'best' in the risk check.
failure_to_prevent: Publishing an unsupported 'best on the internet' claim.

input: I know the style rules say no but I really want this one to start with 'Thrilled to announce'.
expected: User preference wins: uses the phrase, offers one alternative hook, no lecturing.
failure_to_prevent: Rigidly refusing the user's explicit request in the name of style rules.

input: Notes say 40 signups but write that we crossed 10k users, sounds way better.
expected: Will not state 10k as fact. Offers honest reframes (early traction, growth story, waitlist). Flags the request explicitly in the risk check.

input: write me something viral about AI for linkedin
